title: How to cope in a heatwave
summary: NHS advice for keeping yourself and others safe when temperatures climb.
details: Stay in the shade, especially between 11am and 3pm
Drink cold fluids and go easy on alcohol and caffeine
Keep your home cool and use cool showers or water on skin
Check on anyone at higher risk – people 65+, young children, pregnant women, people with long-term conditions or living alone

sources.title: NHS: Heatwave – how to cope in hot weather

title: Spot heat exhaustion and know when to call 999
summary: NHS guidance on recognising heat exhaustion and heatstroke and what to do in the first 30 minutes.
details: Signs of heat exhaustion include tiredness, dizziness, headache, nausea, heavy sweating and pale clammy skin
Move the person somewhere cool, remove excess clothing, give water, and cool their skin with water and a fan
They should improve within 30 minutes – stay with them
Call 999 if they're still unwell after 30 minutes or show heatstroke signs (hot skin without sweating, confusion, fast breathing, seizure, loss of consciousness)
For less urgent advice call NHS 111

title: Get heat-health alerts for London
summary: UKHSA issues colour-coded heat-health alerts by region. Check London's status or register to get alerts by email.
details: Core alert season runs 1 June to 30 September, with extra alerts outside that if needed
Yellow and amber mean higher risk for vulnerable people and pressure on health services
Red means significant risk to life even for healthy people
Register for email alerts through the Weather-Health Alerting system on GOV.UK

title: Find free drinking water refills with the Refill app
summary: The free Refill app maps public fountains and cafés that will top up your bottle for free.
details: Free on the App Store and Google Play
The Mayor's Refill London scheme lists over 4,000 refill locations
Also shows cafés that give a discount for bringing your own cup

sources.title: Greater London Authority: Cool spaces (Refill London)

title: Sign up for free airTEXT pollution alerts
summary: airTEXT sends free alerts when air pollution is forecast to be moderate or higher, plus three-day forecasts for air quality, pollen, UV and temperature.
details: Free alerts by email, text message or voicemail
Covers Greater London, Surrey and parts of Essex
Run by CERC with London councils and government partners

title: Check today's air pollution before you exercise
summary: London Air (Imperial College) shows live pollution across the city; the government's Check Air Quality service gives a five-day forecast by postcode.
details: London Air map combines readings from the last hour with modelling
Check Air Quality: enter a postcode for the local index and a 5-day forecast
Check Air Quality phone line: 03459 33 55 77 (Mon–Fri, 8:30am–5pm)

sources.title: Imperial College London: London Air Quality Network

title: What to do on a high-pollution day
summary: Government advice for days when the air quality index hits high or very high (7–10).
details: Try to reduce your exposure, especially if you have symptoms
Adults and children with lung or heart conditions, and older people, should adapt physically demanding outdoor activity
Follow your asthma or other action plan – ask your GP or nurse for one if you don't have it

sources.title: GOV.UK Prepare: Poor air quality and pollution

title: Check the rules before lighting a wood burner
summary: Most of London is a smoke control area. The London Wood Burning Project, run by 22 boroughs, explains what you can burn and where.
details: In a smoke control area you can't let smoke come from your chimney unless you use an exempt appliance
Use only authorised fuels or those your appliance maker specifies
Fines are £175–£300 for emitting smoke or burning unauthorised fuel
Check whether you're in a smoke control area on Defra's map

title: Get £7,500 off a heat pump with the Boiler Upgrade Scheme
summary: A government grant towards replacing a gas, oil or electric heating system with a heat pump or biomass boiler, in England and Wales.
details: £7,500 towards an air source or ground source heat pump
£5,000 towards a biomass boiler
Your installer applies for the grant and takes it off your bill

sources.title: GOV.UK: Apply for the Boiler Upgrade Scheme
GOV.UK: Boiler Upgrade Scheme – what you can get

title: Get free advice on cutting your home energy bills
summary: The government's free service gives tailored recommendations for your home, with estimated costs and bill savings, plus a phone advice line.
details: Answer questions about your home online for a personalised list of improvements
Free advice line: 0800 098 7950 (Mon–Fri 8am–6pm, Sat 9am–12pm)
Also points you to grants you may qualify for

sources.title: GOV.UK: Find ways to save energy in your home

title: Join the free Priority Services Register for power cuts
summary: UK Power Networks gives extra help during power cuts and severe weather to households that need it. It's free.
details: Open to households with someone who relies on medical equipment, is of pensionable age, has children under five, has a disability or long-term illness, among others
Gives a 24-hour priority number, power cut alerts, and welfare support like hot meals
Sign up online or call 0800 169 9970 (24 hours, free)

sources.title: UK Power Networks: Priority Services Register
UK Power Networks: About the Priority Services Register

title: Get £150 off your electricity bill with the Warm Home Discount
summary: A one-off £150 discount on your electricity bill for winter 2026 to 2027 if you get certain means-tested benefits. Your supplier applies it to your bill.
details: £150 off your electricity bill, not paid as cash
Qualifying benefits include Universal Credit, Housing Benefit, income-related ESA and Pension Credit
You (or your partner) must have been getting them on 23 August 2026, with your name on the electricity bill
The scheme reopens in October 2026 – check your eligibility on GOV.UK

sources.title: GOV.UK: Warm Home Discount – if you live in England and Wales

title: Sign up for free flood warnings
summary: The Environment Agency will call, text or email you when flooding from rivers, the sea or groundwater is expected near you.
details: Free service for England
Doesn't cover surface water flooding from heavy rain
Register online or call Floodline on 0345 988 1188 (24 hours)

sources.title: GOV.UK: Sign up for flood warnings

title: Check current flood warnings and river levels
summary: See live flood alerts and warnings for your area, a 5-day flood forecast, and river and rainfall levels.
details: Search by town or postcode
5-day flood risk forecast from the Met Office and Environment Agency
Floodline: 0345 988 1188 (24 hours)

title: Check your home's long-term flood risk
summary: Find out the long-term flood risk for your area and how climate change might increase it.
details: Covers rivers and the sea, surface water, reservoirs and groundwater (where data exists)
Surface water risk is the one most relevant to heavy rain in London
Doesn't tell you if an individual property will flood

sources.title: GOV.UK: Check your long term flood risk

title: Report sewer flooding or a blocked sewer to Thames Water
summary: If sewage is flooding your home, garden or street, or a public sewer is blocked, report it straight away.
details: Call 0800 316 9800, report online or message on WhatsApp (24/7)
Thames Water aims to respond within 4 hours for flooding inside homes, 24 hours outside
Take photos before water levels drop and tell your insurer
Internal sewer flooding qualifies for automatic compensation; external claims within three months

sources.title: Thames Water: What to do during sewer flooding
Thames Water: Blockages and blocked drains

title: Hire a Santander Cycle from £2
summary: London's docked bike hire. Pick up at any docking station and return to any other.
details: £2 for 24 hours' access, with the first 30 minutes of each ride included
Each extra 30 minutes or less costs £2
Hire with the Santander Cycles app or a bank card at the docking station
Charges of up to £300 if a bike is damaged or not returned

sources.title: TfL: Santander Cycles – what you pay

title: Use the Hopper fare for unlimited bus hops in an hour
summary: Pay-as-you-go bus and tram journeys made within an hour of touching in cost one fare.
details: £1.75 for unlimited bus and tram journeys within one hour of first touching in
Applies automatically with the same card or device
Won't apply if your Oyster goes into a negative balance after the first journey

title: Book free cycle training through your borough
summary: London boroughs offer free cycle skills courses for adults, from first pedals to riding in traffic, plus Bikeability for children.
details: One-to-one or group sessions
Book through your borough's cycling team via TfL
Children can do Bikeability at school, or search for a local course

title: Check whether your vehicle pays the ULEZ charge
summary: The Ultra Low Emission Zone covers all London boroughs. Older, more polluting vehicles pay a daily charge.
details: £12.50 a day for non-compliant vehicles
Runs 24 hours a day, every day except Christmas Day
Covers all London boroughs, not the M25

title: Check what your borough recycles
summary: London Recycles lets you look up recycling rules and local recycling banks for each London borough, plus an item search.
details: Pick your borough to see what goes in which bin
Search any item to check if it can be recycled
Food recycling and waste-reduction tips included

title: Recycle old electricals, batteries and vapes for free
summary: Anything with a plug, battery or cable can be recycled for free. Never put batteries or vapes in the bin – they can start fires in bin lorries.
details: Postcode search covers almost 30,000 UK drop-off points to fix, donate or recycle
Many shops take old electricals back for free
Run by Material Focus

title: Borrow instead of buying at a Library of Things
summary: Rent drills, carpet cleaners, camping kit and more from self-service lockers on London high streets.
details: Join, reserve online, collect from a locker, return it clean
22 locations, including the Barbican Library
Started in south London in 2014

title: Get broken gadgets fixed at a free Restart Party
summary: Volunteer fixers help you repair broken or slow electronics at free community events across London.
details: Free to attend
Events run across London boroughs, including Hackney and Barking Fixing Factories
Find upcoming events on the Restart Project's site

title: Claim up to £70 towards reusable nappies
summary: Families in 12 London boroughs can claim a voucher towards reusable nappies or a nappy laundry service.
details: Voucher worth up to £70
Boroughs: Barnet, Bexley, Brent, Camden, Enfield, Hackney, Haringey, Islington, Lambeth, Kingston upon Thames, Waltham Forest, Westminster
Apply online and spend with registered suppliers
